Container.Name: YunKan-TRT
Container.Overview:
YunKan (云瞰) — self-hosted, local-first **NVR / VMS** for home and small-business IP cameras, with on-device AI: motion, **person / vehicle / face recognition / license plate (ALPR / LPR) / pose & fall / package / baby-cry detection**. Your video stays on your LAN — nothing is uploaded to any vendor cloud. A privacy-first **Frigate / Shinobi / ZoneMinder / Scrypted / Agent DVR / iSpy / MotionEye** alternative — pre-bundled into a single container so there is no Mosquitto / database / reverse-proxy / model-download wiring to do by hand.
This is the **TensorRT variant** — the highest-throughput option for **NVIDIA GPUs** (≥6 GB VRAM recommended; ≥8 GB for many high-resolution cameras). On first start it builds inference engines optimized for your exact GPU — this takes a few extra minutes, one time only; the engines are cached on disk (inside the data directory) and reused across restarts and image updates, rebuilt only if you change the GPU. Pick this over "YunKan-CUDA" when you run many cameras / many AI features on one GPU and want the most headroom. Prefer a no-wait first start, or the engine build fails on an older GPU? Use "YunKan-CUDA" instead — same features, no engine build.
**Prerequisites:** 1. Install the **"NVIDIA Driver"** plugin in Unraid → reboot → `nvidia-smi` works on the host; 2. This template already sets `--runtime=nvidia` and the NVIDIA_* env vars — no extra config needed; 3. This is the largest of the four image variants, so the first pull will take a while.
No NVIDIA GPU? Install "YunKan" (CPU) or "YunKan-OpenVINO" (Intel iGPU). All four variants share the same ports — **only one can run at a time**.
**Works with any RTSP or ONVIF camera** — Reolink, Hikvision, Dahua, Amcrest, Annke, Uniview, EZVIZ, Foscam, Lorex, Anpviz, generic Chinese ONVIF, etc. **Tapo, Wyze, Xiaomi, Eufy, Mi Home, Aqara, Imou** and other proprietary-protocol cameras work via a **go2rtc** bridge. **GB/T 28181 cameras & NVRs** (Hikvision / Dahua / Uniview, etc.) register directly into YunKan — import individual channels, including many NVR channels in one batch.
**Built in:** 24/7 continuous recording + motion-event highlights, **NVR-style multi-camera synced timeline playback**, a **Birdseye** all-cameras overview, **PTZ control with presets**, **virtual tripwires (line-crossing)** for accurate entry/exit direction, customizable **video-wall layouts**, a built-in **file manager** for recordings & snapshots, a **people library** for face recognition, **AI scene understanding** that turns each event into a natural-language summary ("an elderly person fell in the living room" — no OpenAI / Gemini / Claude API keys, all inference on your own GPU), bilingual EN ↔ 中文, **WebRTC (WHEP)** sub-second live streaming with HLS fallback, **two-way talkback** (push-to-talk on supported ONVIF cameras), **Apple Home (HomeKit) incl. HomeKit Secure Video — record motion clips to iCloud (Pro)**, **Home Assistant** integration via MQTT auto-discovery, Web admin + Android + iOS apps, optional off-site backup to **115 网盘 (115 Pan / 115 Cloud)**.
![Dashboard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrtian2016/yunkan-unraid-templates/main/screenshots/dashboard.jpg)
![Events timeline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrtian2016/yunkan-unraid-templates/main/screenshots/events.jpg)
On first launch, open the WebUI to enter the Setup wizard.
Ports (hardcoded): 23406/tcp web dashboard + app API + streaming (required), 23515/udp+tcp low-latency live video, 23880/tcp RTSP for external players (optional), 24214/tcp internal streaming service (no need to expose). Watching from outside your network: enable it in the web interface (Settings, General, HTTPS certificate) - your own domain plus your DNS provider's API key gets a Let's Encrypt certificate automatically over DNS-01 (port 80 stays closed); then pick a public port (23443 by default) and forward that one TCP port. See https://yun-kan.com/docs/remote-access
**Keywords:** NVR, VMS, CCTV, surveillance, security camera, RTSP, ONVIF, IP camera, TensorRT, TRT, CUDA, NVIDIA, GPU, NVDEC, RTX 3060, RTX 4060, RTX 4070, A2000, Tesla T4, motion detection, person detection, vehicle detection, face recognition, license plate recognition, ALPR, LPR, fall detection, pose detection, two-way audio, talkback, 24/7 recording, continuous recording, timeline playback, WebRTC, HLS, Home Assistant, MQTT, smart home, AI NVR, AI camera, AI scene understanding, natural language event summary, smart event description, on-device AI, edge AI, offline AI, no API key, no cloud, privacy, self-hosted, Frigate alternative, Shinobi alternative, ZoneMinder alternative, Scrypted alternative, Agent DVR alternative, iSpy alternative, MotionEye alternative, BlueIris alternative, Reolink, Hikvision, Dahua, Amcrest, Annke, Uniview, EZVIZ, Foscam, Lorex, Tapo, Wyze, Xiaomi, Eufy, Imou, Aqara, HomeKit, Apple Home, HomeKit Secure Video, HKSV, Siri, GB28181, GB/T 28181, birdseye, virtual tripwire, line crossing, entry exit detection, video wall, PTZ, pan tilt zoom, package detection, parcel detection, baby cry detection, people library, NVR playback, multi-channel playback, go2rtc, 云瞰, 摄像头, 监控, 显卡推理, AI 监控, 本地 AI, 自然语言.

### 0.9.44 - **Falls are judged on several signals together** -- this used to be a chain of conditions that all had to hold, and missing any one meant no alert at all. One of them was "we saw this person standing before they went down", which is unavailable in very ordinary situations: someone passes behind furniture and reappears, the system has just restarted, or the person crawls in from outside the frame. Several signals are now weighed together, so one missing piece only lowers the confidence instead of silencing the alert. - **The alert image is the moment of the fall** -- the picture used to be taken when the alert was sent, by which point the person may have got up and walked off. It is now the frame the judgement was made on. - **Event images show the person's posture** -- head, limbs and torso are drawn on fall events, so you can tell at a glance whether the system read the scene correctly. - **Sofas and beds can be excluded from fall alerts** -- detection areas gained a "fall-ignore area": falls are not reported inside it, but people are still detected and faces still recognised. Be careful on beds: someone who rolls into the gap between bed and wall may still count as on the bed. - **The default alerts more readily than before** -- for rooms where people lie down to rest, draw a fall-ignore area or switch the sensitivity to Low. ### 0.9.43 - **Another class of missed falls fixed** -- the previous release only addressed part of this: when the camera is mounted high and someone falls towards it (the most common way people go down in a hallway or corridor) the system still did not recognise it, because a person lying that way looks just as upright in the picture as someone standing. The model that recognises a fallen posture has been replaced, and a fallback that does not depend on posture was added -- if a person's height in the picture collapses and stays down, you get an alert even when the posture cannot be made out. - **Fall settings are down to a single sensitivity** -- there used to be five numbers here, none of which could be judged by feel, and setting one of them too high stopped fall alerts from ever firing. Now there is just High and Low. - **The default is High, so it alerts more readily than before** -- you get an alert whenever someone is on the floor and stays there, even if the fall itself was not caught, because that moment is often hidden by furniture or over between two checks. If it is too chatty (a bedroom camera that sees someone lying in bed, for example), switch the sensitivity to Low. - **NVIDIA graphics users**: after upgrading, run the acceleration step in settings once more, otherwise fall recognition temporarily falls back to a slower path. - **Desktop and classic views no longer disagree about your settings** -- the desktop view could show detection features as enabled while the classic view showed them off. - **The "test" button in automations** no longer sends a message word-for-word identical to notifications you had already received. ### 0.9.42 - **NVIDIA TensorRT users: pose and fall detection were completely non-functional and have been fixed** -- if you accelerated the pose model on the TensorRT page, every inference failed on a dtype mismatch and silently produced nothing. - **Fall alerts actually work now** -- previously, even with fall detection switched on, it almost never triggered because the way a fall was judged broke down on real camera footage. If you had it enabled but never received an alert, it works after upgrading. - **Do Not Disturb no longer swallows fall alerts** -- falls were meant to come through during quiet hours but were being silenced along with everything else, and a fall while getting up at night is exactly the most common case. All other alert types still respect your Do Not Disturb settings. - **Packages at your door stop re-alerting** -- a parcel sitting untouched could previously generate hundreds of "delivered" and "taken" alerts in a single day. It now also considers whether anyone actually passed by and whether that part of the picture really changed. - **New automation actions: DingTalk, WeCom, Feishu/Lark and Bark** -- pick one, paste the bot address and type the message; no more hand-written JSON. Failed deliveries come back with a plain-language reason instead of a bare failure. - **Editing device settings on the web is safer** -- saving one setting could overwrite settings that had just been changed elsewhere (your phone, another tab) back to their old values, for example recording mode silently reverting to "motion only". Only the fields you actually changed are submitted now. - **More stable AI detection and faster snapshots on older Intel integrated graphics** -- on J4125, J4105, N5105 and UHD 630-era chips the system used to enable hardware decoding, but on those chips it is actually slower than plain software decoding, which kept interrupting AI detection and slowed snapshots. It now measures both once at startup and picks whichever is genuinely faster. Newer chips (N100, N305, Iris Xe) are unaffected and keep their existing acceleration.
### 0.9.41 - **Packages at your door are picked up more often** -- deliveries left at the door were frequently missed before; this round of tuning noticeably improves the hit rate. Some camera angles and lower-quality streams will still miss them, and we are continuing to work on it. - **Fewer people mistaken for pets** -- on overhead-angle cameras (hallways, entryways) a person bending or crouching was often labelled a cat or dog; this round reduces those mix-ups, and cats being called dogs happens less often too. Recognition is still being refined. - **Voice announcements work again** -- the spoken announcements in automation rules and the "Test voice announcement" button used to fail; an existing rule that never spoke simply starts working after the upgrade, with no reconfiguration. - **Exported recordings show download progress** -- mobile, web and desktop now show a progress bar and downloaded size while a download runs; previously nothing on screen changed after tapping Download. - **Embed it in the Home Assistant sidebar** -- optional toggle in settings, used together with the SkyView HA integration. ### 0.9.40 - **Leaner, steadier AI detection** -- same all-cameras HD detection at noticeably lower load, with unchanged quality and frame rate. - **No more periodic stutter on flaky cameras** -- cameras on shaky networks recover detection in place, without interrupting or flooding the logs. - **More accurate event timing** -- event and trajectory timestamps now line up with the recording. - **Set camera lights to auto/on/off** -- supported cameras (Hikvision, Dahua, Reolink, TP-Link) expose their supplemental light in settings; AI summaries gain adjustable detail and optional cloud deep analysis. - **TP-Link home cameras (TL-IPC) now supported.** - **Fixes** -- Hikvision IR-only light control, desktop "Go to settings" navigation, event thumbnail aspect ratio, curly quotes on non-Chinese UIs, and upgrade guidance when the docker socket isn't mounted. ### 0.9.39 - **Basic motion detection on the free tier** -- motion detection and push notifications now work without a paid license; the settings pages clearly mark what is free and what needs an upgrade. - **The live wall remembers where you put each camera** -- manually arranged grid positions are saved, and each grid size keeps its own arrangement. - **The AI summary failure alert can be switched off** -- summaries keep retrying on their own and missed events are filled in once the service recovers. - **Fixed a false alarm when saving the remote-access port** -- the port actually worked; only the message was wrong.
### 0.9.38 - **Live video starts much faster on phones away from home** -- iPhones often took ten seconds or more to show a picture (Android was quick); now it appears within a few seconds. - **Settings toggles can be switched off again** -- "IPv6 direct connection" and "automatic HTTPS certificate" could previously only be turned on: the switch showed off and saving reported success, but they stayed on.
### 0.9.37 - **Recognizes your own pets** -- add your cats and dogs and events name the individual animal, with a timeline of where it went during the day, the spots it favors, and a one-line daily recap. Off by default. - **See who visited and where they went** -- the same person appearing on several cameras is merged into a single visit; open it to see which lenses they passed in order, or have YunKan sum up the visit in a sentence. - **A paragraph a day on how things went** -- strangers, packages and falls lead the recap, routine activity is summed up in a line, and a quiet day simply says there was nothing of note. One per day for the whole home. Off by default. - **Movement trails on events** -- the event picture now draws the path the subject took: where they came from, where they went, where they lingered. - **Replay the moment right in the event** -- the event detail plays those few seconds directly, with detection boxes following the action, instead of sending you to the playback timeline. - **HTTPS certificates are issued automatically** -- enter your own domain and YunKan handles issuance and renewal. Port 80 does not need to be open, and 8 DNS providers are supported. Certificates you installed by hand are left untouched. Remote access now needs only one forwarded port, or none at all with IPv6. - **More accurate recognition** -- the recognition model has been replaced across the board: the false alert rate on the same real-world footage drops from 27% to 9%, with a new "highest accuracy" tier for discrete graphics cards. Sheep, cattle and horses are no longer reported as birds. - **Packages are recognized even sitting still** -- previously a package was lost once it stopped moving, and thirty seconds later it was falsely reported as taken. Off by default. - **Push notifications carry the picture** -- the notification shows the subject directly, and the AI summary is folded into that same notification once ready. - **Talk through the camera from the live view** -- type a message and the camera's speaker announces it. - **Other improvements and fixes** -- loitering alerts can skip people you already know; snapshots export in bulk; the event timeline is color-coded by category. Fixes include PTZ cameras panning on a cycle with nobody present, choppy two-way audio on recent TP-Link firmware, a license wrongly reported as revoked when the device clock is off, blurry zoom in the labeling workspace, and a crash on the Pets page. - **UPGRADE NOTE** -- MySQL / MariaDB users: the first startup upgrades one recording table automatically. With a large recording history this takes a few minutes during which the web interface is unavailable; please do not restart midway. It happens only once. SQLite installations are unaffected. If you have trained a custom recognition model, the built-in category system has been updated, so older custom models are marked outdated and YunKan falls back to the built-in model -- retraining once restores it.
### 0.9.36 - **Live streams can be consumed over RTSP by third-party software** such as Home Assistant or go2rtc -- sub-second latency, no segmenting, and the live address published to Home Assistant carries it too. Authentication works exactly as before. - **Far fewer false motion alerts, automatic with nothing to tune** -- shadows and light spots, swaying foliage and rippling water, the timestamp overlay burned into the picture, insects flying close to the lens at night, and the moment the camera switches to night vision are each handled now, while someone walking past with a flashlight still triggers an alert as it should. Detection boxes hug the real subject too, and stray fragments from reflections no longer get a box of their own. - **Fall detection fixed** -- the path that judged the drop leading to a fall had never actually worked, so real falls often went unreported. UPGRADE NOTE: the separate "Pose detection" and "Fall detection" switches are now a single switch, migrated from your existing state; nothing you had disabled gets turned back on for you. - **No more "not a single event" while someone is active at home** -- events now keep coming at a steady pace (every 30 seconds by default) while activity continues. - **H.265 (HEVC) cameras are no longer transcoded to H.264 on the server** -- transcoding permanently occupies one of your graphics card's video encoding channels, so several H.265 cameras viewed at once crowd each other out. YunKan now serves the original video as-is; the mobile apps, Safari and any Chrome / Edge with hardware decoding play H.265 natively. A handful of older browsers without H.265 support can no longer view these cameras on the web. - **Three PTZ fixes** -- direction keys that did nothing at all on some multi-stream cameras now work, the 300 empty factory presets shipped by Hikvision and others are filtered out, and firmware with no preset feature is no longer reported as a fault. - **Resource usage** -- face recognition, AI summaries, HomeKit and the GB/T integration truly stop using memory when switched off (from 100-130 MB down to about 16 MB standby, back within 5 seconds). A new self-check also compares your acceleration settings against what is actually in effect, with guidance for each mismatch. - **Other fixes** -- AI semantic search now states why it is unavailable instead of silently falling back to keyword matching; cameras whose stream vanished and whose recording stopped silently are fixed; and the log center no longer becomes permanently unusable after prolonged use.
### 0.9.35 - **Camera-side detection events now work with any ONVIF camera** -- previously limited to Hikvision, Dahua and Reolink brand APIs. Switch the event source to "Camera" under Cameras / Edit / Camera-side events and the camera's own motion or person detection triggers YunKan events, recordings and alerts, using none of the host's computing power. - **New TP-Link VIGI series support** -- person, motion, tampering, line crossing and area intrusion events plug straight in, with a VIGI brand tile in the add-camera wizard. Also a new "audio anomaly" event category (glass breaking, screaming), kept separate from "crying" so automation rules can react to each differently. - **Two-way talk comes to domestic TP-Link (TL-IPC) cameras** -- these cameras have no public talk interface, so two-way talk was previously unavailable; push-to-talk and automated voice announcements now work, verified on real hardware (their PTZ and other abilities were already supported). - **Two PTZ fixes for every brand** -- cameras added via a brand template or plain RTSP address now have PTZ at all (previously only ONVIF-wizard cameras did), and click-to-aim is no longer wrongly disabled on cameras that never declared their abilities. - **Two-way talk compatibility fix** -- some strict camera firmware silently rejected YunKan's talk audio; affected cameras can talk again. - **"Timestamp repair" upgraded** -- cameras that still dropped frames with the 0.9.34 switch (the Tapo C325WB, for example) are now truly fixed at the source. The switch keeps its name and place; cameras that already have it on pick up the new behavior automatically. - **Existing cameras pick up new abilities without being re-added** -- switching the event source to "Camera" re-probes the camera on the spot and explains clearly when something is genuinely unsupported. - **Clear diagnosis when the integrated GPU cannot be selected for AI detection** -- YunKan now states plainly when the GPU has not been passed through to the container and shows how to fix it; unavailable options are greyed out with a reason.
### 0.9.34 - **New "Timestamp repair" switch fixes dropped frames, artifacts and a misaligned timeline on certain cameras** -- a few cameras (TP-Link's Tapo C325WB, for example) send out-of-order time markers, so recorded clips lose a large share of their frames, show smearing and blocky artifacts, and the playback scrubber does not line up. Turn on Timestamp repair under Cameras / Edit / Connection and YunKan rebuilds the time markers from when each frame actually arrives. Off by default; enabling it briefly reconnects that camera. - **Fixed detection boxes and "crop to the main target" on event images going dead after a while** -- the event images served to Home Assistant, and snapshot previews in push notifications, only drew boxes and applied cropping during a short window right after the event, which is almost never when you actually look at them. ### 0.9.10 (2026-06-01) - **Fixed a regression where some pages could fail to load after upgrading** — a small number of users saw blank "Cameras", "Automations", and "Live" pages after updating from the previous version. This now self-heals on upgrade with no manual action. - **Clearer license plates** — the detection-box outline no longer covers the plate number itself. - **Improved event list** — thumbnails switched to a landscape aspect ratio, plate / face recognition results now show inline in the list, and unread markers are cleaner. - Other fixes: iOS "mark all read" not refreshing the list; smoother web playback timeline dragging (cursor-anchored scroll zoom).
### 0.9.9 (2026-06-01) - **AI scene understanding** — each event gets an automatic natural-language summary ("a person walks up to the door holding a package"), shown on event cards in the web admin and the Android / iOS apps. All inference runs on-box; no OpenAI / Gemini / Claude API key required. - **Smart event search** — search past events by keyword on web and mobile, with semantic matching (searching "delivery" also surfaces "package" events). - **Automatic LAN / WAN switching** — configure both a local and a public address for the same server; the app uses whichever is reachable (LAN at home, public when away), plus a one-tap switch on the home screen. The public live-stream host is now editable in Settings and applies instantly. - **Live detection-box overlay** — overlay recognition boxes and labels (person / vehicle / pet) on the live preview; toggleable on all three clients. - **Lower-latency live streaming** — added a more compatible playback path with automatic best-method selection for smoother live view across more networks. - **Redesigned live view, home, and add / edit-camera screens** on mobile, with full per-camera settings (motion sensitivity, per-class detection toggles, PTZ auto-tracking, offline alerts). - **Cyclist merge** — a person riding a bike / motorcycle is now reported as a single "someone cycling" event instead of separate person + vehicle notifications. - **Push opens the event detail directly**; event snapshots can be saved to the phone album (with boxes / labels); the web event center adds a zoom / pan snapshot viewer. - **Per-camera motion-notification cooldown** for cameras without advanced recognition. - **More accurate license-plate recognition**, especially at distance / under motion blur; plates are merged into the matching vehicle event (one record per car). - **More reliable Android background keep-alive** to reduce missed push on Chinese OEM phones. - **AI summary usage panel** to see processing volume, resource use and success rate. - Stability fixes: camera online / offline false reports, occasionally clipped recording segments, drifting detection boxes, talkback behind a reverse proxy, and a blank "cleanup" log tab; push title / event type / image now stay consistent; fixed duplicate device entries piling up under "bound devices".
### 0.9.8 (2026-05-22) - More accurate recognition (new in-house model) for people, vehicles, bikes, motorcycles, buses, trucks, birds, cats / dogs, and personal items (backpack / handbag / suitcase). - Detection / ignore zones can now apply per object type (e.g. an ignore zone that only ignores vehicles still captures passing people).
Container.Requires: Install the "NVIDIA Driver" plugin so `nvidia-smi` works on the host, otherwise the container can't find CUDA at startup. First start builds GPU-specific inference engines — give it a few extra minutes before adding cameras.

Config.Name: Time zone (TZ)
Config.Description: Container time zone. Affects log timestamps and quiet-hours cron.

Config.Name: Container name (license anchor)
Config.Description: Must exactly match the 'Name' field above. The license heartbeat uses this to identify the container itself; if you rename the container, change this too.

Config.Name: NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES
Config.Description: Which GPU(s) to use. On multi-GPU hosts set this to a specific 'GPU-xxxx' UUID (`nvidia-smi -L` to list); default is all.

Config.Name: NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES
Config.Description: GPU capabilities to enable: compute (CUDA / TensorRT inference) + video (NVDEC hardware decode — note: iGPU + VAAPI actually saves more RAM-copy overhead in practice) + utility (nvidia-smi).

Config.Name: Data directory (DB / config / logs)
Config.Description: Small state: database, config, cookies, logs, upgrade state, and the cached GPU inference engines built on first start. Unraid convention is /mnt/user/appdata/<app>/ (cache pool / SSD recommended). Recordings have their own path entry below — don't size this share for video.

Config.Name: Recordings directory
Config.Description: Camera recordings — can grow to TBs. Mounted on top of the data directory (container path /app/data/recordings), so snapshots / exports / face thumbnails follow it automatically. **To put recordings on a big array share or a dedicated pool, change the host path of THIS entry — do not add your own path mapping with a different container path, it will be silently ignored.** If YunKan already ran on this host and you point this at a new location, FIRST move the contents of .../yunkan/data/recordings/ there — otherwise the old recordings become invisible to the app (playback and auto-cleanup can't see them) while still occupying the data share.

Config.Name: machine-id (license hardware fingerprint)
Config.Description: The license uses the Unraid host's machine-id as part of its hardware fingerprint. **Without this mount the fingerprint drifts on every container recreate; the license then consumes a new activation slot and eventually fails to activate.** Keep read-only.

Config.Name: product_uuid (license hardware fingerprint)
Config.Description: Second hardware-fingerprint signal (motherboard DMI UUID). Keep read-only.

Config.Name: docker socket (self-introspection / OTA self-restart)
Config.Description: YunKan uses the docker socket internally for self-identification and OTA self-restart. The default Unraid permissions are fine.

Config.Name: HTTP / API (nginx)
Config.Description: Web dashboard + REST API front door.

Config.Name: RTSP
Config.Description: Cameras and external players connect directly here.

Config.Name: Internal streaming service
Config.Description: Internal media server (HLS, WebRTC signaling, hooks). Clients never talk to it directly - they go through 23406 with a signed token - so it does not need to be reachable from outside the host.
